assumptions: The upstream provider's outage was inferred from io-shop's own error logs and the absence of any local change; we had no direct telemetry, status page, or confirmation from api.io-pay.example.
Change-event and feature-flag lookups returned nothing for windows up to roughly a week back; we assume those sources are complete and would have shown a deploy or flag change if one had occurred.

The service is assumed to have still been failing at the end of the metrics window, so the outage duration is a lower bound, not a measurement; recovery time and total customer impact are unknown from this record.
Impact is assumed to be limited to account-page rendering (the path that calls card lookup); no other io-shop endpoints were examined.
The one action taken, a process restart, is assumed to have been harmless beyond dropping in-flight requests at 15:25.
input.executive_summary: On the afternoon of 20 September 2026, shoppers could not load their account pages. The pages depend on a third-party payment company's service to show saved card details, and that outside service began refusing requests. Because the page cannot render without it, virtually every attempt to open an account page failed, and the ones that did not fail outright were slow. Before this began, almost all requests were succeeding normally. The problem started at 15:19 UTC, alerting fired about six minutes later, and the pages were still failing at the end of the period we have data for, so we can say the outage lasted at least from 15:19 onward but cannot say from this record when it ended. Automated response picked the incident up immediately, gathered metrics, logs and change history, and confirmed nothing had been deployed or reconfigured on our side. It restarted the service as a precaution; that made no difference, which confirmed the cause was external. With no safe automated action available against a third-party outage, the incident was escalated to humans and a draft code change was opened to make the page degrade gracefully instead of failing entirely when the payment provider is unavailable. Other parts of the shop were not implicated. No data was lost.
input.root_cause: Starting at 15:19 UTC on 2026-09-20, io-shop's upstream payment provider (api.io-pay.example) began returning HTTP 503 for card lookups on /v1/shoppers/{id}/card. Every account-page render depends on that call, so the failure propagated straight through: account-page errors went to effectively all traffic and p50 latency rose to roughly 2s on timeout/retry cost. No deploy, release, or feature-flag change to io-shop appeared in the change history, and restarting the process did not change the behaviour, which places the fault outside io-shop; io-shop's own payment-provider client (src/io_shop/payment_provider.py) has no fallback or circuit breaker for a hard-down provider, so an upstream outage becomes a total outage of the page.
